nodes.raw_latex:
\label{thm:catlin}
	Let $\psi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0}$ and let $\mathcal{K}$ denote the set of $\alpha\in[0,1]$ for which the inequality \eqref{eq:rational approximations again} has infinitely many solutions $(a,q)\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ with $0\leqslant a\leqslant q$. Define $\psi^*:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0}$ by
	\[
	\psi^*(q):=\varphi(q)\sup\{\psi(n)/n \,:\, n\in\mathbb{N},\ q|n\} .
	\]
	Then the following hold:
	\begin{enumerate}[topsep=2pt, itemsep=2pt]
		\item If $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi^*(q)<\infty$, then $\lambda(\mathcal{K})=0$.
		\item If $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi^*(q)=\infty$, then $\lambda(\mathcal{K})=1$.
	\end{enumerate}

Let $\psi$ and $M(q,r)$ be as in as in Lemma \ref{lem:Pollington}, and consider $Y\geqslant X\geqslant1$ such that
\[
1\leqslant \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{\psi(q)\varphi(q)}{q} \leqslant2 .

\eq{\label{eq:E_t}
\mathcal{E}_t 
	= \big\{(v,w)\in (\mathbb{Z}\cap[X,Y])^2 :  \gcd(v,w)\geqslant  t^{-1}\cdot M(v,w) ,\ L_t(v,w)  \geqslant 10 \big\}.

\sum_{(v,w)\in \mathcal{E}_t}  \frac{\varphi(v)\psi(v)}{v}\cdot \frac{\varphi(w)\psi(w)}{w} \ll \frac{1}{t} .

nodes.raw_latex:
We wish to prove that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:MainGoal}
\lambda(\mathcal{A})=1,
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{A}=\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{A}_q$ with $\mathcal{A}_q$ defined by \eqref{eq:A-dfn}. We first  write 
\[
\psi(q)=\psi_1(q)+\psi_2(q),
\qquad\text{where}\qquad
\psi_1(q)
	=\begin{cases}
	\psi(q)&\text{if}\ \psi(q)>1/2,\\
	0&\text{otherwise} .
	\end{cases}
\] 
In particular, $\psi_2(q)=\psi(q)$ if $\psi(q)\leqslant 1/2$, and $\psi_2(q)=0$ otherwise. 

If it so happens that $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_1(q)\varphi(q)/q=\infty$, then we apply Lemma \ref{lem:Large} to $\psi_1$ to find that $\lambda(\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{B}_q)=1$, where $\mathcal{B}_q$ is defined as $\mathcal{A}_q$ but with $\psi$ replaced by $\psi_1$. This proves \eqref{eq:MainGoal}, since $\psi_1(q)\leqslant \psi(q)$, and so $\mathcal{B}_q\subseteq\mathcal{A}_q$.

Therefore we may assume without loss of generality that $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_1(q)\varphi(q)/q<\infty$, and so $\sum_{q=1}^\infty \psi_2(q)\varphi(q)/q=\infty$. 
Thus, we have reduced Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm} to the case when 
\[
\psi(q)\leqslant 1/2\quad\text{for all}\ q\geqslant1. 
\]

By Lemma \ref{lem:Gallagher}, the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture will follow if we prove that $\lambda(\mathcal{A})>0$, 
since this means $\mathcal{A}$ cannot have measure 0. Note that 
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:limsup-rewrite}
\mathcal{A}=\limsup_{q\to\infty}\mathcal{A}_q =  \bigcap_{j=1}^{\infty}
\bigcup_{q\geqslant j}\mathcal{A}_q .
\end{equation}
Now, let $X$ be a large parameter and fix $Y=Y(X)$ to be minimal such that
\[
\sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q} \in[1,2] .
\]
(Such a $Y$ exists since $\psi(q)\leqslant 1/2$ for all $q$.) Hence, we see that it suffices to prove that
\begin{equation}
\lambda\bigg(\bigcup_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \mathcal{A}_q\bigg)\gg1 
\label{eq:Finite}
\end{equation}
uniformly for all large enough $X$, since this implies that $\lambda(\mathcal{A})>0$ by virtue of \eqref{eq:limsup-rewrite}, and hence Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm} follows.

For each $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, consider the counting function
\[  
Q(\alpha)=\#\{q\in\mathbb{Z}\cap [X,Y]: \alpha\in\mathcal{A}_q\} = \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \mathds{1}_{\mathcal{A}_q}(\alpha).
\]
We then have
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{supp}(Q)&=\bigcup_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\mathcal{A}_q,\\
\int_0^1 Q(\alpha) \mathrm{d}\alpha &= \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q) \geqslant \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q} \geqslant 1 ,\\
\int_0^1 Q(\alpha)^2 \mathrm{d}\alpha &= \sum_{X\leqslant q,r \leqslant Y}\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r)  .
\end{align*}
Hence, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality implies that
\[
\lambda\bigg(\bigcup_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\mathcal{A}_q\bigg)\int_0^1 Q(\alpha)^2\mathrm{d}\alpha 
\geqslant\Bigl(\int_0^1Q(\alpha)\mathrm{d} \alpha\Bigr)^2\geqslant1.
\]
Thus, to establish \eqref{eq:Finite}, it is enough to prove that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2ndmoment-goal}
\sum_{X\leqslant q,r\leqslant Y} \lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r) \ll  1 .
\end{equation}
The terms with $q=r$ contribute a total
\[
\sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y}\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q)\leqslant \sum_{X\leqslant q\leqslant Y} \frac{2\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\leqslant 4,
\]
and so we only need to consider the contribution of those terms with $q\ne r$. Applying Lemma \ref{lem:Pollington}, we see that 
\[
\lambda(\mathcal{A}_q\cap \mathcal{A}_r)\ll 
	\mathds{1}_{M(q,r)\geqslant \gcd(q,r)}\cdot \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r}\cdot 
	\prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}} \left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) ,
\]
where we recall that
\[
M(q,r)=\max\{r\psi(q),q\psi(r)\}.
\]
Thus, \eqref{eq:2ndmoment-goal} is reduced to showing that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:goal}
	\sum_{\substack{X\leqslant q,r\leqslant Y \\ M(q,r)\geqslant\gcd(q,r) }} 
		\frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q} \cdot\frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r}
			 \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) \ll 1.
\end{equation}
To prove this inequality, we divide the range of $q$ and $r$ into convenient subsets. 

The pairs $(q,r)\in (\mathbb{Z}\cap [X,Y])^2$ with
\[
 \prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right) < e^{100} 
\]
contribute a total of at most
\[
e^{100}\bigg(\sum_{q\in [X,Y] } 
		\frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\bigg)^2
		\leqslant 4e^{100} 
\]
to the right hand side of \eqref{eq:goal}, and so can be ignored. 

For any other pair $(q,r)$, we see that 
\[
e^{100} \leqslant 
	\prod_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right)
	\leqslant \exp\Bigl(\sum_{\substack{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\frac{1}{p}\Bigr),
\]
so certainly we have
\[
\sum_{p|qr/\gcd(q,r)^2}\frac{1}{p} \geqslant 100.
\]
For any such pair, we let $j=j(q,r)$ be the largest integer such that
\[
\sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j)}} \frac{1}{p}  \geqslant 10. 
\]
Since $j$ is chosen maximally, we have 
\[
\sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j+1)}} \frac{1}{p}  <10 .
\]
Mertens' theorem then implies that 
\[
\sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j)}} \frac{1}{p}=\sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ \exp\exp(j)\leqslant p <\exp\exp(j+1)}} \frac{1}{p}+\sum_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p\geqslant \exp\exp(j+1)}} \frac{1}{p}  \ll 1  .
\]
Therefore
\als{
	\prod_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right)
	&\ll \prod_{M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)<p\leqslant \exp\exp(j)} \left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right)  \\
	&\ll\begin{cases}
		1&\text{if}\ M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)\geqslant  \exp\exp(j),\\
		e^j &\text{otherwise},
	\end{cases}
}
where we used again Mertens' theorem. As above, those pairs with 
\[
\prod_{\substack{p| qr/\gcd(q,r)^2 \\ p>M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)}}\left(1+\frac{1}{p}\right)\ll 1
\]
make an acceptable contribution to \eqref{eq:goal}. Therefore we only need to consider pairs $(q,r)$ with $M(q,r)/\gcd(q,r)<  \exp\exp(j)$.

We have thus reduced \eqref{eq:goal} to showing that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:goal2}
	\sum_{j\geqslant 0} e^j 
	\sum_{(q,r)\in \mathcal{E}_{\exp\exp(j)}} \frac{\varphi(q)\psi(q)}{q}\cdot \frac{\varphi(r)\psi(r)}{r} \ll 1,
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{E}_t$ is defined by \eqref{eq:E_t}. To prove \eqref{eq:goal2}, we apply Proposition \ref{prop:GCD}, which shows that the inner sum is $O(1/\exp\exp(j))$. Since the sum of $e^j/\exp\exp(j)$ over $j\geqslant 0$ converges, this completes the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:MainThm}.

	\[
	\mu(\mathcal{E})\ll 1/t.
	\]

\label{def:special graphs}	
Let $p$ be a prime number, and let $k,\ell\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{V}$ is a set of integers and $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}$, we set
	\[
	\mathcal{V}_{p^k}=\{v\in\mathcal{V}:p^k\|v\},
	\]
that is to say $\mathcal{V}_{p^k}$ is the set of integers in $\mathcal{V}$ whose $p$-adic valuation is exactly $k$. Here we have the understanding that $\mathcal{V}_{p^0}$ denotes the set of $v\in\mathcal{V}$ that are coprime to $p$. In particular, $\mathcal{V}_{2^0}$ and $\mathcal{V}_{3^0}$ denote different sets of integers. 
\item Let $G=(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E})$ be a bipartite graph. If $\mathcal{V}'\subseteq\mathcal{V}$ and $\mathcal{W}'\subseteq\mathcal{W}$, we define
\[
\mathcal{E}(\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}'):=\mathcal{E}\cap(\mathcal{V}'\times\mathcal{W}').
\]
We also write for brevity
\[

Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ be a GCD graph.
\begin{enumerate}
	\item If $\mu(\mathcal{V}),\mu(\mathcal{W})>0$, then we define the \emph{edge density} of $G$ by
	\[
	\delta=\delta(G):=\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E})}{\mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W})}.
	\] 
	If $\mu(\mathcal{V})=0$ or $\mu(\mathcal{W})=0$, we define the edge density of $G$ to be $0$. 
	\item The \emph{neighbourhood sets} are defined by
	\[
	\Gamma_G(v):=\{w\in\mathcal{W}:\,(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}\}\quad\text{for any}\ v\in\mathcal{V},
	\]
and similarly 
\[
\Gamma_G(w):=\{v\in\mathcal{V}:\,(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}\}
\quad\text{for any}\ w\in \mathcal{W}.
\]
	\item We let $\mathcal{R}(G)$ be given by
	\[
	\mathcal{R}(G):= \{p\notin\mathcal{P}: \exists (v,w)\in\mathcal{E}\ \text{such that}\ p|\gcd(v,w)\} .
	\]
	That is to say $\mathcal{R}(G)$ is the set of primes occurring in a GCD which we haven't yet accounted for. We split this into two further subsets:
	\[
	\mathcal{R}^\sharp(G):=\left\{p\in\mathcal{R}(G): 
	\exists k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}\ \text{such that}\ \frac{\mu(\mathcal{V}_{p^k})}{\mu(\mathcal{V})},\frac{\mu(\mathcal{W}_{p^k})}{\mu(\mathcal{W})}\geqslant 1-\frac{10^{40}}{p}\right\}
	\]
	and
	\[
	\mathcal{R}^\flat(G):=\mathcal{R}(G)\setminus \mathcal{R}^\sharp(G).
	\]
	\item The \emph{quality} of $G$ is defined by
	\als{
	q(G)&:= \delta^{10}\mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W})
	\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}} \frac{p^{|f(p)-g(p)|}}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f(p)=g(p)\geqslant1}/p)^2(1-1/p^{31/30})^{10}}, 
}
where $\delta$ is the edge density of $G$. 
\end{enumerate}

Fix $t\geqslant1$ and 
let $G$ be the GCD graph of Proposition \ref{prop:Graph} with set of edges $\mathcal{E}\subseteq\mathcal{E}_t$ (where $\mathcal{E}_t$ is defined in Proposition \ref{prop:GCD}), weight $\mu(v)=\psi(v)\varphi(v)/v$ and edge density $\delta$. 

If $\delta\ll 1/t$, then $\mu(\mathcal{E})\ll 1/t$ and so we are done. Therefore we may assume that 
\[
\delta\geqslant 1/t\quad\text{and}\quad t>10^{2000}.
\] 
Note that this implies that 
\[
t\geqslant 10\delta^{-1/50}.
\]

We apply Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} to $G$ to find a GCD subgraph $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}',\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'$ satisfying either case \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case1} or \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case2} of its statement. In addition, we have that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{R}(G')=\emptyset$;
\item $\mu(\Gamma_{G'}(v))\geqslant(9\delta'/10)\mu(\mathcal{W}')$ for all $v\in\mathcal{V}'$;
\item $\mu(\Gamma_{G'}(w))\geqslant(9\delta'/10)\mu(\mathcal{V}')$ for all $w\in\mathcal{W}'$.
\end{enumerate}
Set
\[
a:=\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{f'(p)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
b:=\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{g'(p)}.
\]
The definition of a GCD graph implies that 
\[
a|v\quad\text{for all}\ v\in\mathcal{V}',
\qquad b|w\quad \text{for all}\ w\in\mathcal{W}'.
\] 
Moreover, since $\mathcal{R}(G')=\emptyset$, and $p^{\min\{f'(p),g'(p)\}}\|\gcd(v,w)$ for all $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'$, we have that 
\[
\gcd(v,w)=\gcd(a,b)
\quad\text{for all}\quad(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'.
\] 

Now, note that
\[
\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{|f'(p)-g'(p)|} = \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}p^{\max\{f'(p),g'(p)\}-\min\{f'(p),g'(p)\}}= \frac{\mathrm{lcm}(a,b)}{\gcd(a,b)}
	= \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} ,
\]
as well as 
\[
\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}\frac{1}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f'(p)=g'(p)\geqslant1}/p)^2(1-1/p^{31/30})^{10}} 
	\ll \prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'}\frac{1}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f'(p)=g'(p)\geqslant1}/p)^2} \leqslant \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)} .
\]
Consequently, from the definition of $q(\cdot)$, we find
\begin{align}
q(G') &=  (\delta')^{10}\mu(\mathcal{V}')\mu(\mathcal{W}')
	\prod_{p\in\mathcal{P}'} \frac{p^{|f'(p)-g'(p)|}}{(1-\mathds{1}_{f'(p)=g'(p)\geqslant1}/p)^2(1-1/p^{31/30})^{10}}\nonumber\\
	& \ll (\delta')^{10} \mu(\mathcal{V}')\mu(\mathcal{W}') \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \cdot  \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)}\nonumber \\
	&= (\delta')^{9}\mu(\mathcal{E}')  \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \cdot  \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)} .\label{eq:QG'Bound}
\end{align}
Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} offers a lower bound on $q(G')/q(G)$. Since
\[
q(G) = \delta^{10} \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{V})= \delta^{9}\mu(\mathcal{E}),
\]
we can obtain an upper bound on the size of $\mu(\mathcal{E})$ by estimating $q(G')$ from above.

\medskip

Note that 
\[
\mathcal{E}'\subseteq\mathcal{E}
\subseteq\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{V}\times\mathcal{V}: M(v,w)\leqslant t\cdot \gcd(v,w)\},
\]
where we recall that $M(v,w)=\max\{v\psi(w),w\psi(v)\}$. 
Since $\gcd(v,w)=\gcd(a,b)$ for all $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'$, we infer that
\[
\psi(v)\leqslant \frac{t\cdot \gcd(a,b)}{w}
\quad\text{and}\quad 
\psi(w)\leqslant \frac{t\cdot \gcd(a,b)}{v}
\quad\text{for all}\quad 
(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'.
\]
The vertex sets $\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{W}'$ are finite sets of positive integers. For each $v\in\mathcal{V}'$, let $w_{\max}(v)$ be the largest integer in $\mathcal{W}'$ such that $(v,w_{\max}(v))\in\mathcal{E}'$. (This quantity is well-defined in virtue of property (b) above. In addition, we emphasise to the reader that `largest' refers to the size of elements as positive integers, and does not depend on the measure $\mu$.) Similarly, for each $w\in\mathcal{W}'$, let $v_{\max}(w)$ be the largest element of $\mathcal{V}'$ such that $(v_{\max}(w),w)\in\mathcal{E}'$. Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{psi ub}
\psi(v)\leqslant \frac{t\cdot \gcd(a,b)}{w_{\max}(v)}
\quad\text{and}\quad 
\psi(w)\leqslant \frac{t\cdot \gcd(a,b)}{v_{\max}(w)}
\quad\text{for all}\quad v\in \mathcal{V}',\,w\in\mathcal{W}'.
\end{equation}


Now, let $w_0$ be the largest integer in $\mathcal{W}'$ and $\mathcal{E}''=\{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}': (v,w_0)\in\mathcal{E}'\}$. We then have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:w0}
w_{\max}(v)=w_0 \quad\text{for all}\quad(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'' .
\end{equation}
In addition, since $G'$ satisfies conditions (b) and (c) in the statement of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges}, we have
\[
\mu(\mathcal{E}'') 
	=\sum_{v\in \Gamma_{G'}(w_0)}\mu(v)\mu(\Gamma_{G'}(v))
	\geqslant \mu(\Gamma_{G'}(w_0))\cdot \frac{9\delta'\mu(\mathcal{W}')}{10}
	\geqslant \bigg(\frac{9\delta'}{10}\bigg)^2 \mu(\mathcal{V}')\mu(\mathcal{W}')\geqslant \frac{\delta'\mu(\mathcal{E}')}{2} .
\]


Substituting this bound into \eqref{eq:QG'Bound}, we find
\begin{equation}\label{eq:q(G') bound}
q(G') \ll (\delta')^{8} \mu(\mathcal{E}'')  \frac{a b}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)}\cdot \frac{a b}{\gcd(a,b)^2} 
	\leqslant \mu(\mathcal{E}'')  \frac{ab}{\gcd(a,b)^2} \cdot \frac{ab}{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)} .
\end{equation}
Here we used the trivial bound $\delta'\leqslant 1$ in the second inequality.
In addition,
\als{
\mu(\mathcal{E}'')  = \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}''} \frac{\psi(v)\varphi(v)}{v} \cdot \frac{\psi(w)\varphi(w)}{w} .
}
Since $a|v$ and $b|w$, we have $\varphi(v)/v\leqslant \varphi(a)/a$ and $\varphi(w)/w\leqslant \varphi(b)/b$. Therefore 
\[
\mu(\mathcal{E}'')\leqslant \frac{\varphi(a)\varphi(b)}{a b}\sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}''}\psi(v)\psi(w).
\]
Together with \eqref{psi ub}, \eqref{eq:w0} and \eqref{eq:q(G') bound}, this implies that
\begin{equation}
q(G') \ll  t^2ab \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}''} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0}  
	\leqslant  t^2ab \sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0}  .
\label{eq:G'Quality}
\end{equation}
We now split our argument depending on whether \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case1} or \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case2} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} holds.

\bigskip

\noindent
\textit{Case 1: \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case1} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} holds.}

\medskip

In this case we have $q(G')\gg \delta t^{50} q(G)$. 
Writing $v=v' a$ and $w=w' b$, we find that
\begin{align*}
\sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0}
&\leqslant \sum_{w'\leqslant w_0/b}\frac{1}{ w_0 v_{\max}(b w')}
	\sum_{v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a}1\\
&\leqslant \sum_{w'\leqslant w_0/b}\frac{1}{ w_0 v_{\max}(b w')}\cdot \frac{v_{\max}(bw')}{a} \\
&\leqslant \frac{1}{ab} .
\end{align*}
Together with \eqref{eq:G'Quality}, this implies that
\[
q(G')\ll t^2.
\]
Since $q(G')\gg \delta t^{50} q(G)$ in this case, and since $\delta \geqslant 1/t$, this gives
\[
\mu(\mathcal{E})  = \delta^{-9}q(G) \ll \delta^{-10}t^{-50}q(G')\ll \frac{1}{\delta^{10}t^{48}} \ll \frac{1}{t} .
\]
This establishes Proposition \ref{prop:Graph} in this case.

\bigskip

\noindent
\textit{Case 2: \ref{prop:Partd}-\ref{prop:Case2} of Proposition \ref{prop:BoundOnEdges} holds.}

\medskip


Write $v=v' a$ and $w=w' b$. In this case 
\begin{equation}
	\label{eq:L_t-lowerbound}
	L_t(v',w')\geqslant 4\quad\text{whenever}\quad(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'.
\end{equation}
We also have $q(G')\gg q(G)$. 

From \eqref{eq:L_t-lowerbound}, we see that either 
\[
\sum_{p|v',\,p\geqslant t}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 2
\quad\text{or}
\quad
\sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}\frac{1}{p}\geqslant 2
\]
whenever $(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'$.
Consequently,
\als{
\sum_{(v,w)\in\mathcal{E}'} \frac{1}{v_{\max}(w) w_0}  
	&\leqslant  \mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b,\ v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a\\ \sum_{p|v' w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 4}}  \frac{1}{v_{\max}(b w') w_0}  \\
	&\leqslant S_1+S_2,
}
where
\begin{align*}
S_1&=\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b,\ v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a\\ \sum_{p|v',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}}  \frac{1}{v_{\max}(b w') w_0} ,\\
S_2&=\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b,\ v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a\\ \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}}  \frac{1}{v_{\max}(b w') w_0}  .
\end{align*}
For $S_1$, we note that 
\als{
S_1&\leqslant \sum_{w'\leqslant w_0/b} \frac{1}{w_0v_{\max}(b w')} \sum_{\substack{v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a \\ \sum_{p|v',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} 1\\
	&\ll \sum_{w'\leqslant w_0/b} \frac{1}{w_0v_{\max}(b w')} \cdot \frac{v_{\max}(b w')/a}{t^2e^t} \\
	&\leqslant \frac{1}{ab t^2e^t} 
}
by Lemma \ref{lem:Anatomy}, since $\exp(t^e)\gg\exp(t)t^2$. 
Similarly for $S_2$, we find that
\als{
S_2&\leqslant\sum_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b \\ \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} \frac{1}{w_0v_{\max}(b w')} \sum_{v'\leqslant v_{\max}(b w')/a}1\\
	&\leqslant \sum_{\substack{w'\leqslant w_0/b \\ \sum_{p|w',\,p\geqslant t}1/p\geqslant 2}} \frac{1}{aw_0} \\
	&\ll \frac{1}{ab t^2e^t} ,
}
by applying Lemma \ref{lem:Anatomy} once again. Substituting these bounds into \eqref{eq:G'Quality}, we conclude that
\[
q(G') \ll e^{-t}.
\]
Since we have $q(G)\ll q(G')$ and $\delta\geqslant 1/t$, this gives
\[
\mu(\mathcal{E})  = \delta^{-9}q(G) \ll t^{9} q(G')\ll t^{9} e^{-t} \ll 1/t. 
\]
This establishes Proposition \ref{prop:Graph} in all cases.

\label{prop:IterationStep1}
Let $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ be a GCD graph with edge density $\delta>0$ such that 
\[
\mathcal{R}(G)\subseteq\{p>10^{2000}\}\quad\text{and}\quad \mathcal{R}^\flat(G)\neq\emptyset.
\] 
Then there is a GCD subgraph $G'$ of $G$ with edge density $\delta'>0$ and multiplicative data $(\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ such that
	\[
	\mathcal{P}\subsetneq\mathcal{P}'\subseteq\mathcal{P}\cup\mathcal{R}(G),
	\quad
	\mathcal{R}(G')\subsetneq \mathcal{R}(G),
	\quad 
	\min\bigg\{1,\frac{\delta'}{\delta}\bigg\} \cdot \frac{q(G')}{q(G)}\geqslant 2^N ,
	\]
	where $N=\#\{p\in\mathcal{P}'\setminus \mathcal{P}:f'(p)\neq g'(p)\}$.

\medskip

\begin{equation}

\quad q(G^{(1)})\geqslant\frac{q(G)}{10^{10^{3000}}}
\quad\text{and}\quad

\label{eq:G1Quality}
\end{equation}

\[

\] 
until we obtain a GCD subgraph $G^{(2)}$ of $G^{(1)}$ which does not satisfy the conditions of Proposition \ref{prop:IterationStep1}. \]

\[

q(G^{(2)})\geqslant \frac{2^N}{10^{10^{3000}}} \cdot q(G)
\quad\text{and}\quad  
\delta^{(2)}q(G^{(2)})\geqslant

\[
\mathcal{R}(G^{(3\text{a})})=\emptyset

We then consider $G'=(\mu,\mathcal{V}\setminus\{v\},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E}',\mathcal{P},f,g)$, which is a GCD subgraph of $G$. Let $G'$ have edge density $\delta'$. We claim that $\delta'\geqslant \delta$ and $q(G')\geqslant q(G)$.

Indeed, we have
\als{
\mu(\mathcal{E}')
	= \mu(\mathcal{E})-\mu(v)\mu(\Gamma_G(v)) 
	&\geqslant \delta \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W})-\frac{9\delta}{10}\mu(v)\mu(\mathcal{W}) \\
	&=\delta \big(\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)\big)\mu(\mathcal{W})\cdot\Big(1+\frac{\mu(v)/10}{\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)}\Big).
}
Thus the edge density $\delta'$ of $G'$ satisfies
\[
\delta'=\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E}')}{\mu(\mathcal{V}\setminus\{v\})\mu(\mathcal{W})}
		=\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E}')}{\big(\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)\big)\mu(\mathcal{W})}
		\geqslant \delta\cdot \Bigl(1+\frac{\mu(v)/10}{\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)}\Bigr).
\]
Thus we see that $\delta'\geqslant \delta$, and that 
\begin{align*}
(\delta')^{10}\mu(\mathcal{V}\setminus\{v\})\mu(\mathcal{W})
	&\geqslant \delta^{10}\big(\mu(\mathcal{V})-\mu(v)\big)\mu(\mathcal{W})

		= \delta^{10} \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W}) .
\end{align*}
This proves our claim that $q(G')\geqslant q(G)$ too, thus completing the proof of the lemma.

Note that if $(k,\ell)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}^2\setminus \mathcal{X}$, then $\mu(\mathcal{E}_{p^k,p^\ell})\leqslant \mu(\mathcal{V}_{p^k})\mu(\mathcal{W}_{p^\ell})=\alpha_k\beta_\ell \mu(\mathcal{V})\mu(\mathcal{W})=0$. Thus $\sum_{(k,\ell)\in \mathcal{X}}\mu(\mathcal{E}_{p^k,p^\ell}) = \mu(\mathcal{E})$. Hence, if we assume that the inequality in the statement of the lemma does not hold for any pair $(k,\ell)\in \mathcal{X}$, we must have
\[
1=\sum_{(k,\ell)\in\mathcal{X}}\frac{\mu(\mathcal{E}_{p^k,p^\ell})}{\mu(\mathcal{E})}< S_1+S_2,
\]
	where

	S_1:=\sum_{k=0}^\infty(\alpha_k\beta_k)^{9/10}
	\]
	and

	S_2:=\sum_{\substack{k,\ell\geqslant0\\ k\neq\ell}}
		\frac{\alpha_k(1-\beta_k)

			+\alpha_\ell(1-\beta_\ell)
			+\beta_\ell(1-\alpha_\ell)}{2^{|k-\ell|/20}\times 1000}.
	\]
Thus, to arrive at a contradiction, it suffices to show that
	\[
	S_1+S_2\leqslant 1.
	\]
First of all, note that $\sum_{|j|\geqslant1}2^{-|j|/20}=2/(2^{1/20}-1)\leqslant 100$, whence	
\begin{align*}
S_2&\leqslant 
	\frac{1}{10}
		\bigg(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k(1-\beta_k)
		+\sum_{k=0}^\infty\beta_k(1-\alpha_k)
		+\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\alpha_\ell(1-\beta_\ell)
		+\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\beta_\ell(1-\alpha_\ell)\bigg) \\
	&=\frac{1}{5}\bigg(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k(1-\beta_k)
		+ \sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\beta_\ell(1-\alpha_\ell)\bigg).
\end{align*}
Observing that 
\[
1-\beta_k=\sum_{\ell\geqslant0,\ \ell\neq k} \beta_\ell
\quad\text{and}\quad
1-\alpha_\ell=\sum_{k\geqslant0,\ k\neq \ell} \alpha_k,
\]
we conclude that
\[
S_2\leqslant \frac{2}{5}\sum_{\substack{k,\ell\geqslant0\\ k\neq\ell}} \alpha_k\beta_\ell.
\]

Since $\alpha_k,\beta_\ell$ are non-negative reals which sum to 1, there exists some $k_0\geqslant0$ such that 
\[
\gamma:=\max_{k\geqslant0}\alpha_k\beta_k= \alpha_{k_0}\beta_{k_0}.
\]
We thus find that 
\[
S_1 = \sum_{k=0}^\infty(\alpha_k\beta_k)^{9/10}\leqslant \gamma^{2/5}\sum_{k=0}^\infty(\alpha_k\beta_k)^{1/2}\leqslant \gamma^{2/5}\Bigl(\sum_{k=0}^\infty \alpha_k\Bigr)^{1/2}\Bigl(\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}\beta_\ell\Bigr)^{1/2}= \gamma^{2/5}
\]
where we used the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to bound $\sum_k (\alpha_k\beta_k)^{1/2}$ from above. 
We also find that
\[
\frac{5 S_2}{2}\leqslant \sum_{\substack{k,\ell\geqslant0\\ k\neq\ell}} \alpha_k\beta_\ell
	= 1- \sum_{k=0}^\infty \alpha_k\beta_k
	\leqslant 1-\gamma.
\]
As a consequence, 
\[
S_1+S_2\leqslant \gamma^{2/5}+\frac{2}{5}(1-\gamma).
\]
The function $x\mapsto x^{2/5}+2(1-x)/5$ is increasing for $0\leqslant x\leqslant1$, and so maximized at $x=1$. Thus we infer that $S_1+S_2\leqslant1$ as required, completing the proof of the lemma.

\label{lem:MainLem}
Consider a GCD graph $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ with edge density $\delta>0$ and a prime $p\in\mathcal{R}(G)$ with $p>10^{40}$. Then one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a GCD subgraph $G'$ of $G$ with multiplicative data $(\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ and edge density $\delta'>0$ such that
\[
\mathcal{P}'=\mathcal{P}\cup\{p\},\quad
\mathcal{R}(G')\subseteq \mathcal{R}(G)\setminus\{p\},\quad 
\min\bigg\{1,\frac{\delta'}{\delta}\bigg\}
	\cdot \frac{q(G')}{q(G)} \geqslant 2^{\mathds{1}_{f'(p)\neq g'(p)}} .
\]
\item There is some $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}$ such that
\[
\frac{\mu(\mathcal{V}_{p^k})}{\mu(\mathcal{V})}\geqslant1-\frac{10^{40}}{p}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{\mu(\mathcal{W}_{p^k})}{\mu(\mathcal{W})}\geqslant 1-\frac{10^{40}}{p}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

\label{lem:SmallPrime}
Consider a GCD graph $G=(\mu,\mathcal{V},\mathcal{W},\mathcal{E},\mathcal{P},f,g)$ with edge density $\delta>0$, and let $p\in\mathcal{R}(G)$ be a prime. Then one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a GCD subgraph $G'$ of $G$ with multiplicative data $(\mathcal{P}',f',g')$ and edge density $\delta'>0$ such that
\[
\mathcal{P}'=\mathcal{P}\cup\{p\},\quad
\mathcal{R}(G')\subseteq\mathcal{R}(G)\setminus\{p\},\quad 
\min\bigg\{1,\frac{\delta'}{\delta}\bigg\}
	\cdot \frac{q(G')}{q(G)} \geqslant \frac{1}{10^{40}} .
\]
\item There is some $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant0}$ such that
\[
\frac{\mu(\mathcal{V}_{p^k})}{\mu(\mathcal{V})}\geqslant \frac{9}{10}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{\mu(\mathcal{W}_{p^k})}{\mu(\mathcal{W})}\geqslant \frac{9}{10}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

nodes.raw_latex: On the other hand, if we count integers $v$ with weight $\mu(v)=\varphi(v)/v$, then the set $\mathcal{S}$ we defined above has total weight $\mu(\mathcal{S})\asymp x^c/\log{n}$, and so it fails to be of a sufficiently large size unless we take $n$ bounded (in which case the prime $p$ is of size $\asymp x^{1-c}$ and it divides a positive proportion of the elements of $\mathcal{S}$).
